title: I open-sourced ~2,000 more dead crypto bots. My "best" ideas did no better than my random ones😭
author: drykilo
selftext:
I've been building a pipeline that tests crypto trading strategies hard, because 99% of "my bot made 80% in backtest with 10 Sharpe" posts are either grifters or posters who have never heard about overfitting, never facing real tests.  
  
Every strategy I write goes through 7 stages on real Binance data:   
**Code safety check->In-sample->Out-of-sample->Walk-forward->Randomized start dates->Slippage stress test->Final holdout slice that nothing sees**.   


This is a pipelline I have been imroving based on feedback from Reddit. Fail one stage and it's over for your bot. Every bot gets a report card showing exactly which stage killed it. This batch: \~1,980 strategies. I came up with the ideas and the tests, AI wrote most of the code (\~80%). 6 survived...That's 0.3%.  


[github.com/CacheCarti/Crypto-Strategies](http://github.com/CacheCarti/Crypto-Strategies)   
  
The repo already had 748 bots from earlier batches. This adds \~1,970 more, each with its code and report card. 2732 bots in total  


Some things I found:   


* Split the batch into **exploit** (variations of ideas that had already worked), **explore** (new ideas), and **wildcard** (weird random stuff).
* Pass rates: Exploit passed 4 of \~1,200, explore 1 of 500, wildcard 1 of 300 (aimed ideas did about as well as random weird ones😭😭😭😭, though 6 survivors is a tiny sample).
* Ran 500 random coin-flip bots through the exact same pipeline to check if the screen is just letting noise through: 0 of 500 passed.
* Fees are modeled: 4bps taker plus impact and spread on every trade.
* Almost everything died at out-of-sample (a backtest looking great and then dying on unseen data is the most common story here).
* **What this does NOT show:**
   * The card screen only uses 6 months of data as a cheap first filter, not the final exam. The 6 survivors go through 6+ years and a 2.75-year combined test before anything else, and they stay private.
   * A bot passing the screen doesn't mean it makes money; it means it hasn't been caught yet.

  
The validator is open source now too: pip install dmoera, then dmoera validate. Run it on your own strategies and see where they die.   
  
If you think a test is missing, please tell me. Every suggestion so far has killed more of my bots. That's the process :)!
